acceptance_evidence: AC1, kpi.json carries every field: verify-delivery writes it from the same measure the report uses, and this ticket's own delivery produces one
AC2, the weekly report covers every ticket delivered that week: docs/harness/reports/2026-W39.md lists all eight with median cycle time, rework, findings by severity and points
AC3, the sprint report compares planned against delivered: sprint-0 reads 27 of 77 points, and the eval pass rate is reported as not yet measurable rather than as zero
AC4, a fix ticket increments escaped defects: test_a_fix_ticket_increments_escaped_defects_on_what_it_fixed, with a fixture ticket naming an earlier one
AC5, no report can carry a credential: test_a_report_carrying_a_credential_is_refused, using the same rule as the journal
The retrospective requirement: the first report covers eight tickets that predate it, including SEEN-086 which has no journal

findings.claim: The append-only proof treated every file in a journal directory as a record
findings.failure_scenario: kpi.json is rewritten whenever a ticket delivers again, which is exactly what a reopen leads to, so doctor reported a rewritten record and CI refused the delivery. Any ticket that reopens could never deliver, which makes the reopen SEEN-093 added unusable
findings.resolution: The proof covers NNNN.json records; kpi.json and attachments are the allowlisted files beside them. A genuinely edited record is still caught, with a test for each. Reopened at record 25, red at 26 against the unfixed code, green at 27

findings.claim: verify-merge refused a report regenerated after the receipt
findings.failure_scenario: The week a ticket delivers in includes that ticket, so the report moves at delivery. Every ticket from here would have been refused at the merge check for doing the normal thing, and the workaround would be to skip verify-merge, which is the one control standing in for branch protection
findings.resolution: Reports join the journal, the coverage baseline and the graph as things delivery writes. Any other change after the receipt is still refused. Found by the check refusing this ticket's own merge; reopened at record 16, red at 17, green at 18

findings.claim: Findings were counted once per review record, so a returned ticket multiplied its own findings
findings.failure_scenario: SEEN-090 reported thirty findings from nine, because four reviews each listed the same set. Every KPI derived from findings would be wrong in proportion to how much a ticket was reworked, which inverts the measure: the tickets that were reviewed most carefully would look the worst
findings.resolution: Findings are counted by id with the most recent record winning, so a finding resolved on the second pass is one finding. Red at 8, green at 9

findings.claim: A report reading only kpi.json files would have covered nothing
findings.failure_scenario: Eight tickets had delivered before this one, none with a kpi.json, so the first weekly report would have been empty while the work sat in the tree, and nobody would have trusted the second one either
findings.resolution: The journal is the source and kpi.json is a cache. Found by the clarify gate refusing three times, and recorded at record 2

findings.claim: Reports and kpi.json were inside the reviewed-tree fingerprint
findings.failure_scenario: Running harness report would change the tree a receipt attested, so a report could refuse a delivery, and delivery writing kpi.json would invalidate its own receipt. The coverage baseline did exactly this in SEEN-089
findings.resolution: Both sit outside the fingerprint, with a test. Named in the solution record before it was written, which is the first time this class of bug was caught before it happened

findings.claim: First-pass CI is null for every ticket delivered so far
findings.failure_scenario: A KPI that reads null for eight tickets looks like a measure nobody implemented
findings.resolution: verify-delivery records the checks it verifies from now on, and the report's last section names the field as not yet measurable with the reason. Guessing a value for the eight would have been worse than saying so

security_checklist: Reports are refused when they carry an environment value, by the same rule as the journal
The session log reader takes four token counts and nothing else: a log holds prompts and file contents that do not belong in a journal
No PII, no database, no agent action
